planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; part-shade siting mutes the gold color slightly but keeps foliage from scorching in hot climates.

directions: Nugget is an older, cold-hardy gold-leaf ninebark selection out of South Dakota, with foliage that emerges rich butter-yellow in spring, mellows to lime-green through summer heat, and returns to gold in fall before dropping to expose cinnamon-colored exfoliating bark for winter interest. Small white spring flower clusters attract pollinators and give way to reddish seed capsules that persist into fall. It shrugs off clay, drought, rocky soil, and harsh prairie winters better than most gold-foliage shrubs, making it a reliable choice where newer compact cultivars struggle with hardiness. Renewal-prune by removing about a quarter of the oldest stems at the base each year to maintain a full, vigorous habit and the brightest new growth color.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained to moist soil; foliage holds its brightest gold color in a half-day-sun to partial-shade spot and stays greener in deeper shade.

directions: Honeybee is a compact, mounded selection of the southern Appalachian native bush honeysuckle, prized for lance-shaped foliage that emerges bright chartreuse-gold and holds its color through the growing season rather than fading to green like many yellow-leaved shrubs. Clusters of tubular, nectar-rich yellow flowers open in early summer against the gold foliage and draw bees and the occasional hummingbird. Slow-spreading by suckers, it forms a tidy low colony well suited to a woodland-edge border or shaded mass planting, and tolerates heat, humidity, and dry shade with little fuss once established. Little pruning is needed beyond an occasional light shearing after the main spring flush to keep the mound dense and the new growth brightest.
